articles.title: Gaza declares epidemic alert after meningitis claimed 15 lives
articles.author: Aseel Saleh
articles.content_excerpt: On Tuesday, November 24, the Ministry of Health in the Gaza Strip declared an “epidemic alert” across all governorates, after 1,790 meningitis cases were recorded, adding that at least 15 people had died from the infectious disease. The ministry warned of an increase in fatalities due to meningitis, particularly among children. It attributed the surge in cases to the repercussions of Israel’s genocidal aggression against Gaza and its continued ban on the entry of medicine and other essential supplies into the war-ravaged territory. articles.title: Israeli forces raid Al-Ama’ri Refugee Camp, detain dozens of Palestinians
articles.author: Aseel Saleh
articles.content_excerpt: On Monday, November 23, the Israeli military stormed Al-Ama’ri refugee camp in Al-Bireh city in the central occupied West Bank. During the hours-long raid, Israeli forces converted the Al-Ama’ri Youth Center, alongside several residential homes, into temporary detention and field interrogation sites. They also damaged the facilities of the center. 30 Palestinians were briefly detained and interrogated after their homes were raided, but were released before the military left the camp. However, one Palestinian young man was arrested in the assault, during which stun grenades and tear gas were fired. articles.title: Too Big to Fire? Jensen Huang Is Back at Nvidia; Questions Loom Over AI Boom & U.S.-China Relations
articles.content_excerpt: Nvidia stock prices surged over 30% on Monday as the chip maker reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO . Huang had stepped down earlier in November amid reports he had multiple extramarital affairs, including with a woman accused of spying for China. Huang and Nvidia have been central to the AI boom, and the leadership turmoil had erased trillions in value from the U.S. stock market. President Donald Trump acknowledged he had encouraged the company’s board to bring Huang back. “The fact that our markets are so over-indexed on the AI trade, that something like three-fourths of gains in the [S&P 500] this past year have been AI-related, is unsustainable,” says Aya Ibrahim, senior fellow for economic and national security at the AI Now Institute. articles.title: ICE Out of NJ Demands Freedom for Junior Marte & Other Former Delaney Hall Hunger Strikers
articles.content_excerpt: Democracy Now! has obtained exclusive audio from inside Delaney Hall, the controversial immigrant detention center in Newark, New Jersey, operated by the for-profit prison company GEO Group. The audio was recorded over the summer during a labor and hunger strike organized by immigrant detainees. Junior Marte, an asylum seeker and father from Venezuela, was one of the organizers. He describes conditions inside the facility, including abusive treatment, medical neglect and prolonged legal limbo. “We are here unjustly, wrongfully accused of being criminals. Yet immigration officials refuse to review our cases, because they know that we are all innocent people,” Marte says in the message. articles.author: BreakThrough News
articles.content_excerpt: On November 12, the campaigns for Ecuador’s local elections formally began. This Sunday, November 29, voters will elect prefects, mayors, city council members, and members of local boards. Historically, local elections have reflected the level of support or opposition to the current government. In this sense, right-wing president Daniel Noboa has more at stake than just a simple popular election. This is especially true when considering the last elections (which centered on four referendum questions) held on November 16, 2025.
